note: HEREDOC QUOTING BIT TWICE IN ONE SESSION WRITING COMMIT MESSAGES, IN TWO DIFFERENT WAYS. (1) A commit message passed as git commit -m  DIES on an apostrophe inside the message when the outer context is single-quoted — bash reports unexpected EOF while looking for matching quote and nothing commits. (2) Worse because it SUCCEEDS: a subagent using the same shape got a stray literal EOF and ) appended after the Claude-Session trailer, producing a corrupt but committed message. The second failure is the dangerous one, since the commit lands and looks fine in --oneline. WHAT WORKS RELIABLY: write the message to a scratch file and use git commit -F <file>, or git commit --file=- with a plain quoted heredoc on stdin. Both survive apostrophes, parentheses and trailers with no escaping. Relevant to anyone dispatching subagents that commit: put the -F form in the dispatch prompt rather than leaving the agent to improvise, because failure mode (2) is silent.
